item.title: CAN questions conviction of Christian woman in Borno
item.description: …Raises religious freedom concerns By Luminous Jannamike The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) has faulted the reported conviction and imprisonment of a Christian woman in Borno State, raising concerns over religious freedom and the protection of fundamental rights. The woman, identified in circulating reports as Lami Samuel Dawa, was reportedly convicted in a case said to have involved the conversion of an adult woman to Christianity. CAN said the precise facts and legal basis of the conviction were still being verified. In a statement by its President, Archbishop Daniel Okoh, the association disclosed that an appeal had been filed, adding that it was committed to allowing the judicial process to run its course. “The Association believes that every individual has the right to freely choose, change or practise their religion or belief without coercion, intimidation or unlawful punishment,” CAN said. The association urged the relevant authorities to protect the rights of all parties and ensure that justice was served in accordance with the Constitution and the law. CAN also pledged to monitor developments and engage the authorities through appropriate legal and institutional channels, while reaffirming its commitment to peaceful coexistence among Nigerians of different religious backgrounds. It said the case highlighted the need to protect the fundamental rights and freedoms guaranteed to every citizen, including the right to freely choose and practise a religion. Amupitan noted that the Osun election recorded the highest voter turnout in the history of off-cycle elections in the state and was adjudged locally and internationally as credible despite earlier security concerns. He said: “Osun State elections gave us the confidence that we can achieve this despite the noise. It is good that we had a series of those elections before the general elections because we learn lessons from every election.” He added that INEC would use the experience gained from the off-cycle elections to improve its preparations for the 2027 polls, noting that the commission was determined to conduct elections that would advance the country rather than create further challenges. item.title: Aston Villa to take legal action against pundit Carragher
item.description: Aston Villa have announced plans to take legal action against former Liverpool defender-turned-pundit Jamie Carragher for what the club described as “unacceptable insults” about the club and its supporters. Carragher, a prominent pundit with Sky Sports and CBS, has been hit with a backlash by Villa fans for suggesting that manager Unai Emery should be a candidate to replace the under-fire Michael Carrick at Manchester United. “Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the club and its fans,” Villa chairman Nassef Sawiris said in a short statement posted on the club’s social media feeds. “Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football.” Emery has transformed Villa’s fortunes since taking charge four years ago. The Spaniard has led the Birmingham-based club twice into the Champions League and ended a 30-year wait for silverware by winning the Europa League last season. However, he has had to build a new team this season after six of the side that started the Europa League final departed in the transfer market, seeking either higher wages or the chance to challenge more routinely for silverware. Emery also enjoyed success at Valencia and Sevilla, but struggled with higher demands in spells at Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal. “Surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again. There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not,” Carragher told the Stick to Football podcast. “Aston Villa will never be Manchester United.” AFP The post Aston Villa to take legal action against pundit Carragher appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Sowore reacts as Ekiti police arrest 11 over attack
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Ekiti State Police Command has arrested 11 suspects over the attack on African Action Congress (AAC) presidential aspirant, Omoyele Sowore, and members of his team at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, the state capital. In a statement on Saturday, the command’s Public Relations Officer, Abutu Sunday, said operatives of the Rapid Response Squad arrested the suspects at their hideouts in the Atikankan area of the town at about 10pm on Friday, following a tip-off. It partly reads, “The Ekiti State Police Command has arrested eleven (11) suspects in connection with the alleged attack on Mr Omoyele Sowore, an African Action Congress (AAC) presidential aspirant, and other persons at Tawakalitu Restaurant, Dalimore Area of Ado-Ekiti. “The suspects are Joseph Tayo ’32yrs’, Olatunji Abayomi ’41yrs’, Isaac Amba ’22yrs’, Kehinde Ajigbana ’18yrs’, Tosin David ’18yrs’, Solomon Iyanu ’18yrs’, Ogunsola Ayomide ’21yrs’, Ojo Ayodeji ’22yrs’, Kayode Dada ’32yrs’, Segun Olatunji ’28yrs’ and Salami Emmanuel ’53yrs’. “Items recovered include two walkie-talkies, substances suspected to be Indian hemp and Colorado, two Indian hemp crushers, one pack of Rizla, seven ATM cards, thirteen mobile phones, two vehicle keys, one flash drive, one 5G MTN Wi-Fi device, identity cards, eight international passports, three complimentary cards, two suspected criminal charms, one gas lighter and ₦250.” The police said investigations were ongoing to establish the individual roles of the suspects and determine their possible connections with the attack. The Commissioner of Police, Falade Michael, assured residents that everyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The statement quoted him as saying that the command “will leave no stone unturned in ensuring that all those found culpable are brought to justice.” Reacting to the arrests, Sowore demanded that the alleged masterminds and sponsors of the attack be identified and brought to justice, insisting that the incident was a coordinated assault and not an ordinary altercation. The presidential candidate made the demand in a post on X on Saturday, describing the arrests as an admission that the incident was a violent attack. He also alleged that some of the attackers were associated with the City Boys group and called for investigations into possible links between the incident and officials of the state government. Sowore urged the Commissioner of Police, Falade Adegoroye Michael, and the Department of State Services to preserve and release CCTV footage from the scene to help identify those involved. “Arresting 11 suspects is not enough if those who planned, financed, coordinated and facilitated the attack remain untouched,” he wrote. He also demanded an explanation from the police over their initial description of the incident as an altercation. item.title: Iran’s supreme leader warns US, Israel against new attacks
item.description: Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei on Saturday warned the United States and Israel against returning to war, according to a written statement, following threats from the Islamic republic’s foes of a possible resumption of strikes. “If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for ending them,” said a statement attributed to Khamenei posted on his website. The remarks came during a reported meeting between Khamenei and senior military commanders, including armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi. It was the first reported meeting between them. Khamenei has not been publicly seen since he became supreme leader, following his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s killing in US-Israeli strikes at the start of the Middle East war in February. According to the statement, Khamenei ordered the commanders to ensure that “any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response”. It also said that Khamenei ordered the commanders to update Iran’s target list to include “all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy”. The war began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which swiftly responded with attacks on countries around the region. The supreme leader’s statement came as fresh diplomatic efforts were under way to avert a resumption of fighting. A Qatari delegation arrived in Tehran on Friday for talks with Iranian officials, after Iran reportedly received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance. According to Iranian media, Tehran had yet to respond to the letter. The post Iran’s supreme leader warns US, Israel against new attacks appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu hails BusinessDay publisher Frank Aigbogun at 70
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has congratulated the Publisher of BusinessDay newspaper, Frank Aigbogun, on his 70th birthday, praising his contributions to business journalism, economic reporting and national development. Tinubu described Aigbogun as a distinguished journalist and media entrepreneur whose work has helped promote informed public discourse and strengthen business reporting in Nigeria. The president conveyed his congratulations in a statement dated October 31, 2026, ahead of Aigbogun’s birthday on Sunday, November 1. He commended the veteran journalist for his commitment to responsible journalism and for using BusinessDay to provide a platform for insightful analysis of economic policies, investment opportunities and developments shaping the country’s business environment. Tinubu said, “As a distinguished journalist and media entrepreneur, Aigbogun has contributed significantly to the growth of business journalism, economic reporting, and informed public discourse in Nigeria.” He also acknowledged the newspaper’s role in connecting different stakeholders in the country’s economic sector. “Of particular note is his use of BusinessDay to strengthen connections among the media, the private sector, policymakers, and the investing public, while advancing credible business reporting in national development,” the president stated. Tinubu further described experienced media professionals such as Aigbogun as important contributors to Nigeria’s institutional development, particularly as the country implements economic reforms. “I believe experienced media professionals such as Frank must remain invaluable contributors to Nigeria’s institutional development and the advancement of business journalism, at a critical time, as our nation undergoes economic reforms,” he said. The president also praised Aigbogun’s commitment to providing insightful coverage of economic policies and investment opportunities, noting the importance of credible business journalism to national development. “As he celebrates this milestone, I wish him good health, renewed strength, and greater accomplishments in the years ahead,” Tinubu added. item.title: UK PM ‘open’ to slavery apology but not reparations
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Saturday he was “open” to the UK issuing a formal apology for its role in the transatlantic slave trade, but ruled out financial reparations. The Labour leader made the remarks days before attending a Commonwealth leaders summit in Antigua and Barbuda, as King Charles III tours the Caribbean. “I want to express my sorrow and regret for the pain and suffering of so many millions and to recognise the way it still shapes our world today,” Burnam wrote in the Guardian newspaper. The transatlantic slave trade was a “brutal and barbaric violation” of the rights of those enslaved, he said. The British premier added his government wanted a “structured dialogue with those affected”. “Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of this process and I am open to them.” The king is due to address the Commonwealth summit, which runs from November 1 to 4. Britain’s central role in slavery and the treatment of people in its former colonies has loomed over the 77-year-old monarch’s Caribbean tour. In the Bahamas on Tuesday, Charles acknowledged “the great suffering of the past” during the first leg of his visit. Britain has never formally apologised for slavery or agreed to pay reparations. item.description: An important decision on governorship candidates, fresh pressure over the voters’ register, and a new battle for the South-East have shifted the 2027 campaign into more consequential territory. INEC says it examined the complaints against relevant records and legal provisions. In Gombe, Pantami’s successful petition offers the PDP an opportunity to compete with a candidate whose exclusion had threatened its position in the state. Unless the decision is overturned through a lawful process, the PDP faces the prospect of contesting the wider election without its preferred governorship candidate on the ballot. That could have consequences beyond the governorship race. State-level campaigns help mobilise supporters for other elections. They provide organisational networks, local leadership and political visibility. A party without a governorship candidate may find it more difficult to sustain enthusiasm among its supporters. But there is also a larger principle. Political parties cannot demand strict compliance with electoral law from INEC while treating their own statutory obligations as optional. If the law requires membership registers to be submitted within a prescribed period, parties must comply. Equally, INEC must demonstrate that it applies those requirements fairly to every party, whether ruling or opposition. The commission’s willingness to uphold some petitions and reject others is evidence of a review process. It is not, by itself, proof that every decision was correct. That judgment must rest on the law, the records and, where necessary, the courts. item.title: Iran’s army warns any new US attack would spread war wider
item.description: Iran’s army warned Saturday that any new US attack would only spread their war wider, following threats by America and Israel of further military action as they hold crucial elections. The Iranian warning comes with fresh diplomatic efforts underway to avert a resumption of fighting, with Qatari mediators in Tehran and US Vice President JD Vance reportedly sending a letter to Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei. “If the US president once again embarks on more regional adventurism under pressure from, and in an attempt to appease, the Zionists, the flames of war will undoubtedly engulf a much wider geographical area,” Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said in a post on X, without elaborating. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi also warned on Saturday that “Iran’s Powerful Armed Forces will deal against those who dare harm our people”. On Friday, a Qatari delegation arrived in the Iranian capital for talks with senior Iranian officials. Qatar and Pakistan have been mediating between the warring parties, but the talks have yet to produce a lasting agreement. The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Vance had sent his letter to Iran’s security chief at the direction of President Donald Trump in a bid to revive negotiations and avert further US strikes. Iran has confirmed receiving the letter but has not announced any response. The US holds midterm elections on Tuesday that could determine the direction of the war, which has proven unpopular with American voters following a spike in energy prices due to the conflict. Last Tuesday, Israel also held legislative elections, with voters given a chance to offer a verdict on right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Under Netanyahu, who has vowed to topple Iran’s government, Israel and Iran have engaged in direct military confrontations after decades of shadow war. The Middle East war began in late February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran that killed the country’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei as well as senior military commanders. Iran in response targeted US assets across the Middle East as well as Israel. Most recently hostilities have focused on the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial Gulf shipping route for energy exports that Iran has blockaded since the start of the war. The US has in retaliation been blockading Iranian ports in an attempt to squeeze the nation’s economy. item.title: ONSA, DSS Rescue Three Zamfara Clerics Kidnapped En Route To Prayer Session For Tinubu
item.description: The Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) and the Department of State Services (DSS), in collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, have rescued three Islamic clerics kidnapped while travelling to attend a special prayer session for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in Zamfara State. The victims were among six Imams abducted on September 12, 2026, when heavily armed bandits intercepted them at about 11:30 a.m. along the Dakko-Damri feeder road, near Sububu Forest in Bakura Local Government Area, about three kilometres from Damri village, at Gidan Suleiman Bature. The clerics, identified among the group as Imam Yahuza, Magawata Abdullahi, Malam Shehu Dakko, Imam Bala Fagon and Na’ibi Tasi’u, were reportedly travelling to Talata Mafara for a special prayer gathering seeking divine guidance and favour for President Tinubu’s administration and political future. Following the abduction, the kidnappers reportedly demanded a ransom of 30 million naira for their release. A senior security operative involved in the operation confirmed in Gusau that three of the clerics were rescued unharmed following a series of intelligence-led operations. The rescued clerics subsequently underwent medical examinations and security debriefings. They are said to be in stable condition and are expected to be formally handed over to the Zamfara State Government for reunification with their families. item.title: Navy marines kill 34 terrorists, disrupt ISWAP/Boko Haram operations in Lake Chad
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Nigerian Navy Marines at the Naval Base Lake Chad in conjunction with 403 Amphibious Brigade Nigerian Army, operating under Operation Hadin Kai, have recorded significant operational gains against Boko Haram Terrorists (BHT) in the Lake Chad area, neutralising 34 ISWAP/Boko Haram terrorists in the waters. Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, Director of Information while making this known on Saturday said the operation was conducted through intelligence-driven offensive. He said, “On 28 October 2026, the Nigerian Navy Marines conducted offensive operations against terrorist elements, with initial reports indicating that 8 terrorists were killed in action. “A subsequent Battle Damage Assessment revised the casualty figure to 28 terrorists killed in action. “In a separate operation on 30 October 2026, the Nigerian Navy Marines deployed at Naval Base Lake Chad conducted an offensive strike against identified Boko Haram terrorist enclave at Dumba. “The operation followed Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance missions that facilitated the identification and monitoring of terrorist elements before a precision strike was executed. “Preliminary Battle Damage Assessment indicates that approximately 6 terrorists were neutralised, while several others reportedly sustained injuries. “The casualty figures remain subject to further verification as operational assessments continue. “Since their deployment, the recently established Nigerian Navy Marines have served as a force multiplier under Operation Hadin Kai, strengthening the conduct of offensive operations against terrorist elements. “Their operational contributions have enhanced the capacity to target terrorist enclaves, disrupt hostile activities and deny Boko Haram Terrorists freedom of action within the Lake Chad area. “These efforts continue to support the degradation of terrorist capabilities and advance ongoing operations to restore peace and stability in the North East. “The Nigerian Navy remains committed to supporting joint operations through sustained offensive action and intelligence-driven engagements to strengthen national security and protect vulnerable communities.” The post Navy marines kill 34 terrorists, disrupt ISWAP/Boko Haram operations in Lake Chad appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Senegal kicks off Youth Games, Africa’s first ever Olympics
item.description: The 2026 Youth Olympic Games, the first Olympics ever to be held on African soil, open Saturday in the Senegalese capital marking an historic moment for the continent. Signs proclaiming “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates” are abundant across Dakar, which is hosting some 2,665 young competitors aged 14 to 17 from around the world. The event marks the return of Russian athletes to the Olympics and also includes a refugee team. Overall, the athletes will compete across 25 sports and 153 medal events. “We’ve got people from around the world that maybe had a very different idea about Africa and they’re going to leave, hopefully, with something really positive in mind”, International Olympic Committee (IOC) President Kirsty Coventry, a former Zimbabwean swimmer, said Thursday during a press conference in Dakar. “I think that is really important for our continent”, she said. Events ranging from athletics to beach wrestling, rugby sevens to breaking, will be held across eight venues in three locations. Dakar, the nearby suburb of Diamniadio and the beach town of Saly located some 80 kilometres (50 miles) from the capital, will all host events. – Sports culture – An opening ceremony Saturday evening in Diamniadio will kick off the Games. A total of 136 Senegalese athletes will participate in the Youth Olympics, with some 6,000 volunteers from Senegal helping put on the event. The west African nation is renowned for its sports culture, including its football team, traditional wrestling and surf scene. Football enthusiasts and young people often organise impromptu matches in the evenings or weekends on the beach or in village squares. And as the day cools, hundreds of people flock to Dakar’s iconic coastal road, the Corniche, to run, do strength training or take part in group exercise. While a sense of excitement is beginning to stir in the capital, the fourth summer edition of the Youth Olympics have struggled to stoke wild enthusiasm across Senegal. Many are more concerned with the high cost of living, unemployment and economic hardship. “Once the youth Olympic Games in Senegal begin, Dakar will become the capital of African youth,” Senegal Prime Minister Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo said in an interview with AFP this week. “Africa hosting the (Youth) Olympic Games, it’s a symbol”, he said. – Russian athletes – With the IOC effectively lifting the Russian Olympic Committee’s (ROC) suspension in July, the Youth Games will mark the first Olympic competition since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in early 2022 in which Russian athletes are allowed to compete under their own flag and colours. item.title: US, S/Korea, Japan vow ‘complete’ N/Korea denuclearization
item.description: The United States, South Korea and Japan reaffirmed their commitment to the “complete denuclearization” of North Korea on Saturday, as Pyongyang continues to reject disarmament ahead of possible talks with Washington. Speculation is mounting over a potential meeting between US President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un at next month’s APEC summit in China, with Trump making repeated overtures to Pyongyang for nuclear talks. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and his Japanese counterpart Toshimitsu Motegi “reaffirmed their resolute commitment to the complete denuclearization” of North Korea during talks on Friday on the sidelines of a Group of 20 (G20) meeting in Atlanta in the US state of Georgia, the US State Department said. They also pledged “full implementation” of UN Security Council resolutions, including a ban on supporting revenue for North Korea’s nuclear and ballistic missile programmes. Despite long-running UN sanctions, North Korea, which is backed by Russia and China, has enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state in law, with its regime repeatedly declaring its atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible. – Open to meeting – Trump has made repeated overtures to Pyongyang for nuclear talks, while scaling back joint military drills with ally South Korea. The mercurial US leader even bucked long-held US policy last year by conceding that North Korea was already “sort of a nuclear power”, while reaching out to Pyongyang for talks, saying he was “100 percent” open to a meeting — a suggestion that went unanswered. Analysts and South Korea’s spy agency say Kim may have conveyed Pyongyang’s position on potential talks with Trump to Beijing during a recent visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong. South Korea’s dovish President Lee Jae Myung — who has repeatedly offered Pyongyang talks without preconditions — suggested in September that Washington seek a freeze, rather than the immediate elimination, of the North’s nuclear programme in return for sanctions relief. Critics have said such an approach risks tacitly accepting North Korea as a nuclear-armed state while allowing Pyongyang to win sanctions relief without giving up its arsenal. Analysts say China may also be moving towards tacit acceptance, pointing to the omission of North Korean denuclearisation from statements after Kim and Chinese President Xi Jinping met in June. Pyongyang denounced a joint statement on Saturday by a group of nations monitoring sanctions implementations against it, vowing that “the stereotyped sanctions racket of the US and the West can neither influence the position of the DPRK (North Korea) as a nuclear weapons state”. item.title: NYSC Members Kidnap: ‘I didn’t know my passengers had AK-47 rifles – Okadaman tells court
item.description: By Chidi Nkwopara A commercial motorcycle rider (okadama) has told the court that he was unaware that his passengers, two of the suspected October 1 kidnappers of prospective members of the National Youths Service Corps, NYSC, had AK-47 rifles in a bag. Read Also: NYSC kidnap: DSS witness exposes how suspects were identified The Department of State Services, DSS, on Friday, called two witnesses in the ongoing suit, HOU/22C/2026, filed against Usman Aliyu, Mohamed Aliyu and Babangida Ali, over the kidnap of 20 prospective NYSC members. The graduates were travelling to their orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. Led in evidence by the Principal State Counsel, Mr. Ekezie Nwauzor, the second prosecution witness, PW2, a commercial motorcyclist, Mr. Light Timothy, gave a graphic account of how the first and second accused persons hired him to take them to where their colleagues were staying. According to PW2, his two passengers were carrying a bag, which he never knew the content until they reached their lonely destination, where AK-47 rifles were brought out from it. He recalled that when his passenger put a call to someone, his intonation sounded Hausa or Fulani and the fellow urged him to ply the Umuguma-Okuku Road in Owerri West Local Government Area of Imo State. PW2 also told the court that at a point, fear gripped him and he wanted to go back but not long after, four men jumped out of the bush, collected the bag, opened it and brought out the AK-47 rifles. Timothy also told the court that he would have been killed for wasting time on the road, if not that one of them pleaded on his behalf and he sped off from that point. In his own evidence, the third prosecution witness, PW3, and Akwa Ibom Transport Company driver, Mr. Sunday Udoh, confirmed that he and another driver, Jeremiah, were carrying NYSC members from Ibadan, to their orientation camps. They had a stopover at Onitsha and left 5.30am on October 1, 2026, adding that heading towards Owerri and not long after passing a checkpoint, he noticed two stationary mini buses. He told the court that on sensing looming danger and he quickly tried to reverse but his vehicle hit something behind and they were stuck. According to Udoh, he switched off his vehicle, ran to the other side of the highway, hid in the nearby bush and watched events from there. Udoh, after identifying Usman Aliyu as one of the attackers, also said that the kidnappers took away five of his passengers and 15 from Jeremiah’s bus, into the bush. After thorough cross-examination of the two witnesses by the defence counsel, Paschal Ofoma, Justice Emeka Orafu adjourned the matter for further hearing to November 3, 2026. Though disagreement on the interpretation and authority of Hadith has long existed among Muslim scholars, Masussuka’s unique stance on the matter placed him at odds with scholars who considered his teachings inconsistent with established Islamic traditions. Amid growing scrutiny of his preaching, the Katsina State Government, on November 18, 2025, announced that Masussuka would be required to defend his teachings before a committee of Islamic scholars established based on the several calls. The meeting, however, didn’t see the light of day due to undisclosed circumstances, as he continued to challenge other sects that go against his ideologies. Sources close to the late cleric revealed that his doctrine attracted several death threats, but he didn’t take them seriously as he restrained his followers from reacting. His killing has left many questions amid renewed concern over the safety of clerics across the northern region. Masussuka’s murder was not the first in the North. Over the years, prominent Islamic clerics like late Sheikh Umaru Dan Me Shiyya, Sheikh Jafar Mahmud Adam and Sheikh Auwal Albani Zaria were all victims of cold-blooded murder. A day after his killing, Boko Haram breakaway group, Ansaru, took responsibility for the attack in a viral audio clip. A security analyst, Dr Audu Bulama Bukarti, also linked the cleric’s killing to Ansaru, noting that the released audio had been confirmed to be from the Ansaru group. But Masussuka’s family has rejected the claim and questioned the authenticity of the audio. Childhood The late cleric was born in Yauyau village in the present-day Batsari Local Government Area to a family of pastoralists. His parents relocated to Masussuka in Ningi Local Government Area of Bauchi State when he was a toddler. He started his Qur’anic education in Masussuka village before he left for other towns and villages and returned to Katsina in search of Islamic knowledge. He attended the Arabic Teachers College in Katsina, but dropped out and went to Malam Zakariya Qur’anic School in Sabuwar Unguwa area of the state. Malam Ismail Zakariya, the son of his late teacher (Malam Zakariya) and proprietor of the school, told Weekend Trust that the cleric stayed at the school for about seven years before he relocated to Dutsin-Ma town. According to Ismail, Masussuka, besides his persistent pursuit of Islamic knowledge, was highly entrepreneurial, dealing in traditional medicines (local herbs) to sustain himself and his family. He recalled the late cleric was arrested at the height of Boko Haram in 2000, on the suspicion that he had links with some terror groups. He was later absolved of the allegation and released unconditionally. “My father, Malam Zakariya, engaged the security agency then and secured his release. The allegation prevented Masussuka from securing a house in Katsina City and he decided to leave Katsina for Dutsin-Ma,” Ismail said. Ismail stated that those who disagreed with Masussuka’s preaching do so for selfish reasons. He said, “Everyone knows the Qur’an is one scripture that cannot be altered, but what matters is the interpretation depending on how one views it and the nature of the audience. “Hadith is the only point of contention between the Qur’aniyyun sect and the Muslims from the other sects and even those who believe in Hadith have admitted that some are prescribed as weak and others as genuine and authenticated. “To me, the approach Masussuka adopted in explaining and interpreting those portions during preachings earned him more enemies than followers, but beyond that, there is nothing different from what other Muslim scholars preached,” he said. He respected me as a teacher and a father,” Adam said. According to him, many scholars who opposed Masussuka’s preaching did so “out of hatred for the truth.” According to him, “he may be wrong in his approach to presentation or interpretation as a human being, but I can tell you for free that Masussuka never compromised, saying things as they are and that could be the reason he earned more enemies. This, notwithstanding, we celebrate the truth he preached,” Adam added. He was also a man of wisdom. He established two schools in Dutsin-Ma. One purely focuses on teaching the Islamic religion, while the other focuses on both formal and non-formal education. “What keeps coming to my mind is Masussuka’s persistent pursuit of education and his willingness to impart the same to younger generations. item.title: Parallel campaigns within APC
item.description: While the All Progressives Congress (APC) officially kicked off its presidential campaign last week, a major hindrance to its effective spread in all the geopolitical zones and states in the country has remained the lack of synergy in many states. Weekend Trust checks revealed that there are many states where leaders of the party claiming to work for the reelection of its presidential candidate, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, prefer to work in isolated camps, without as much as involving other leaders in its operations. This, our correspondent learnt, is due to unresolved leadership disputes, personality clashes and the bid outdo each other to prove the one with the bigger political worth. The intensity, however, varies in degree from state to state, with some openly defying each other, while some put up a façade of working together, but beneath the surface are trying to undermine each other’s efforts. Masari, who is considered one of the influential APC figures in Katsina, was absent during the inauguration of the Dikko/Tinubu Campaign Council by Governor Dikko Umaru Radda. He was also missing at the official flag-off of the campaign in Funtua Local Government Area. However, rather than joining the governor at the public campaign events, Masari is said to have intensified separate political consultations within and outside Katsina State ahead of the 2027 general elections. His recent engagements suggest efforts to build support for the Tinubu-Radda re-election project through religious leaders, academics, former political office holders, grassroots organisations, party stakeholders, community influencers and members of the business community. On October 26, Masari held a meeting with 1,121 Islamic clerics in Katsina, comprising members of the Qadiriyya and Tijjaniyya orders, the Izala movement, as well as male, female and youth Islamic scholars. At the meeting, he reportedly appealed to the religious leaders to communicate their positions to their congregations and encourage eligible voters to support President Tinubu. Similarly, on October 9, Masari was among prominent Katsina political figures who attended a high-level APC stakeholders’ meeting convened by Governor Radda at the Katsina State Governor’s Lodge in Abuja. Although details of the discussions were not made public, the meeting was held behind closed doors amid preparations by the ruling party for the 2027 elections. Earlier, on October 2, Masari inaugurated two political support organisations in Katsina: the Wazirin Tinubu Ambassador Movement and the 360Plus1 Support. The initiatives were reportedly designed to strengthen grassroots mobilisation for the Tinubu-Radda ticket. He also received the leadership of the Joint Islamic First Aid Organisation in Abuja during the same month. The delegation was led by its chairman, Ahmad Jingi Adamu. Masari had also engaged senior academics from universities across the country in September 2026 during a high-level meeting themed, “Consolidating the Renewed Hope Agenda: Three Years of President Tinubu’s Achievements and the Road to 2027.” In another political engagement, he addressed thousands of APC supporters and political stakeholders at Nabanje, his hometown in Kafur Local Government Area, as part of efforts to consolidate support for the ruling party. Interestingly, despite the inauguration of the main Dikko/Tinubu Campaign Council, Governor Radda also inaugurated an Independent Campaign Council (ICC) on October 28, 2026, in what appears to be another mobilisation structure ahead of the elections. At the inauguration, Radda expressed confidence in the APC’s preparedness for the 2027 general elections and urged the council’s officials and members to work harmoniously with other political groups within the party to achieve their objectives across the state’s 34 local government areas. The ICC Director-General, Abubakar Abdullahi-Matazu, disclosed that the council had established a five-member structure for each polling unit across the state to strengthen its grassroots presence ahead of the elections. However, political analyst Ahmad Aminu Malwa believes that the true state of affairs within the Katsina APC may not become clear until after the presidential election. According to him, it is only then that the underlying disagreements, political rivalries and other issues within the party may fully emerge into the public domain. “With all the visible indicators showing the existing rift between the two Katsina APC big wigs and taking into consideration the INEC’s elections timetable, it will be very difficult to see the real misunderstanding indices between the two, but believe me, whatsoever is the issue, it will be visible after the presidential election,” he said.
